rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent split-wing mass in all four views, so it does not fail on view coherence. It does, however, feel under-anchored as a neighborhood living building: the dominant form is a compact abstract cluster rather than a clearly programmed street building with one primary occupiable body, active ground threshold, and a legible public void. The blue frontage edge is acknowledged, but the response is still semantically weak—the ground plane does not open decisively toward access, and the split produces more object-like separation than a meaningful court or entry seam. The silhouette is serviceable but not especially strong as a capacity-bearing section; the upper massing is somewhat arbitrary and the section logic is not yet doing program work. Compared with the similar references, it needs a clearer public void and a more legible base/upper hierarchy. Compared with the counterfactual, it borrows some terracing/bridge language but lacks the continuous inhabited section that would justify it for this program.
